hypothesis: The vulnerability is in AtomicQueue.solve() (verified source, compiler 0.8.21+commit.d9974bed, contract 0xd45884b592e316eb816199615a95c182f75dea07): the `solver` argument is caller-supplied and never checked against msg.sender, and the second loop calls want.safeTransferFrom(solver, users[i], assetsToUser), pulling the WANT token out of the named solver via solver's standing approval to the queue
falsification_test: fetch the verified source of 0xd45884b592e316eb816199615a95c182f75dea07 and read solve(), a require(solver==msg.sender) or an absence of the transferFrom(solver,...) leg would invalidate this

hypothesis: The attack path can only reach a `solver` that has code, because solve() calls IAtomicSolver(solver).finishSolve(...), a high-level Solidity call that reverts on a code-less address, consistent with this, all 11 drained wallets have code (seven are 23-byte EIP-7702 delegations beginning 0xef0100, four are proxy contracts)
falsification_test: call eth_getCode on each of the 11 victims at block 25952624, any drained wallet returning 0x (no code) would invalidate the "code required" claim
